title: 113 Species classification and determination of forage mass of bermudagrass pastures overseeded with cool-season annual grasses and legumes and rye-ryegrass winter pastures using Sentinel-2 images
content:
Abstract
Understanding the dynamics of forage biomass and species composition is essential for optimizing grazing management and improving the sustainability of livestock production systems. Recent advances in remote sensing, particularly the availability of high-resolution satellite imagery such as Sentinel-2, offer promising alternatives for large-scale and accurate monitoring of pastures. Therefore, this study evaluated the use of Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and machine learning algorithms to estimate forage mass and classify pasture types in bermudagrass pastures overseeded with cool-season annual grasses and legumes, as well as rye-ryegrass winter pastures. The experimental area was at the Texas A&M AgriLife Research and Extension Center in Overton, Texas. Forage samples were collected from 2018 to 2024. Forage mass was determined by hand-clipping to ground level, followed by drying to obtain dry matter content. Sentinel-2 images were processed using Google Earth Engine (GEE) to extract relevant spectral and vegetation indices. Pastures were classified into four categories: bermudagrass + clover, bermudagrass + ryegrass, bermudagrass, and rye-ryegrass. Two machine learning algorithms, Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost, were tested for pasture classification and forage mass estimation. The RF algorithm achieved an accuracy of 0.76 for pasture classification, slightly outperforming XGBoost, which achieved an accuracy of 0.73. For forage mass estimation, the RF model demonstrated superior performance with an R² of 0.83, root mean square error (RMSE) of 9.28 g/m² and mean absolute error (MAE) of 56.64 g/m². In comparison, the XGBoost model achieved an R² of 0.80, RMSE of 9.72 g/m², and MAE of 65.83 g/m². These results highlight the potential of integrating Sentinel-2 satellite imagery with machine learning algorithms for practical and reliable forage mass estimation and pasture classification. The RF algorithm demonstrated better overall performance for both tasks, providing a reliable tool for pasture management decision-making. This approach offers a scalable and cost-effective solution for monitoring and managing grazing systems, contributing to improved sustainability and productivity in pasture-based livestock systems.
